title: Tag the 19 controls in our control library by category and type
situation: Our control library lists 19 security measures in plain sentences, from firewall rules to door locks to a weekly manager review of login reports. Auditors want each one tagged two ways: what kind of control it is, and what job it does. One entry is just a note about our cloud platform and may not be a control at all.
your_task: Read each control description and match key phrases to a category: technical, physical, managerial or operational.
Match key phrases to a type: preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, compensating or directive.
Leave any entry with no matching phrases as Unclassified for a person to review.
Compare your tags with the answer key and record the score.
why_it_matters: Auditors check that every risk has controls that prevent, detect and correct problems. A library with wrong labels hides gaps, such as having lots of detection but nothing that fixes the damage afterward.
done_when: All 19 controls are tagged with a category and type, with the phrases that support each tag.
Entries with no supporting evidence are marked Unclassified instead of guessed.
Tags match the answer key, and identity controls (such as login logging and the weekly login report review) are listed for the IAM team's access review evidence.

glossary.Control category: Who or what carries out the control: technology, a physical object, management policy, or people following a procedure.
glossary.Preventive control: Stops a problem before it happens, like a door lock.
glossary.Detective control: Spots a problem while or after it happens, like a log or motion sensor.
glossary.Corrective control: Fixes the damage after a problem, like restoring from backup.
glossary.Compensating control: A substitute used when the normal control is not possible.
glossary.Directive control: Tells people what they must or must not do, like a policy or sign.

talking_point: Classified 19 security controls by category and type with 19/19 agreement with the answer key, and left the one entry with no supporting evidence as Unclassified for human review instead of guessing.
